title: [finding] the declared `previousValues` form key reaches the DOM as an unknown React prop (warning on every ObjectForm header render)
body:
Observed while running `packages/plugin-form` tests for #6372 / #6371. Not caused by that work — it reproduces on unmodified `origin/main` @ `631d81dbf`.

## Fact

Rendering `object-master-detail-form` (which composes `<ObjectForm>` for its header) emits, on stderr:

```
React does not recognize the `previousValues` prop on a DOM element. If you intentionally
want it to appear in the DOM as a custom attribute, spell it as lowercase `previousvalues`
instead. If you accidentally passed it from a parent component, remove it from the DOM element.
```

Reproduced from `packages/plugin-form/src/MasterDetailForm.detailSchemaFetchFailure.test.tsx` (any test in the file; the warning is emitted once per fresh render of the header form).

## Where it comes from

`previousValues` is a **declared schema key**, not a stray prop:

- `packages/types/src/form.ts:1101` — `previousValues?: Record<string, any>;`
- `packages/types/src/zod/form.zod.ts:624` — mirrored in the zod schema
- `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx:978-979` — destructured with a comment pointing at objectui#3484

So the value is authored metadata that is reaching the DOM through a spread rather than being consumed and dropped. React then declines it and prints the notice — i.e. the prop is silently **not doing anything** at that DOM node, whatever it was meant to do further up.

## Why it is worth a card rather than a shrug

The failure direction is the quiet one. A declared key that leaks to the DOM is a key whose consumer either does not exist or is being bypassed on this path; the console notice is the only signal, and console notices in a test suite are routinely read as noise. Whether `previousValues` is genuinely consumed on the master-detail header path is the thing to check — the answer decides whether this is a spread hygiene fix or a dead declared key.

Distinct from #6033, which covers `previousValues` only as one row in a zod-mirror drift census; this is the runtime DOM leak.

Filed unassigned for triage. Severity is a triage call: nothing user-visible, but it is either a spread bug or an inert declared key.
